rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: slice-by-what-you-learn.md:6 'Cut across the whole journey instead, so the slice works end to end and the test means something' — closest to a loose referent: 'journey' and 'test' resolve to the customer's journey named at you-specify-it-builds.md:4 and the assumption test named at slice-by-what-you-learn.md:4; you-specify-it-builds.md:6 'build it and check it' resolves to the idea/slice in the same chunk. Harm (unresolvable referent) absent.

you-specify-it-builds.md:6 'Nobody can hand the agent that knowledge' is the nearest to a pointer; it resolves inside the chunk (para 1 names the knowledge). No 'the opening lecture' style callbacks anywhere.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: slice-by-what-you-learn.md:4 'the part the roadmap lists first' is the nearest; 'the roadmap' is a generic product artefact, not a did/saw/caught beat. No 'you did/saw' references in either chunk.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.

rules_evaluated.evidence: you-specify-it-builds.md:4 'Specifying well is the harder half: which customer, which step...' — each chunk (119 and 111 words incl. header) carries a self-contained claim; neither is a wait-state.

Chunk 1 header 'Specifying what to build is now the harder half' vs you-specify-it-builds.md:4 'Specifying well is the harder half'; chunk 2 header 'The first slice tests what you are least sure of' vs slice-by-what-you-learn.md:4 'the first slice tests the assumption you are least sure of'. Both true summaries.

slice-by-what-you-learn.md:4 'Not the easiest part, not the part the roadmap lists first.' is the closest to the 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' tic, but the claim comes first and the two negations follow as a pair, so it is not the banned order and each negation carries concrete content. grep for superlatives ('most useful|best|key to') -> 0; no triples, no number+retraction, no abstraction-noun stacks, no verb triplets.
